newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard returns three rafters to Cuba. [CORRECTED 23:18 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard returns three rafters to Cuba. [CORRECTED 23:18 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Monday repatriated three Cubans who were picked up in the Florida Strait fleeing the communist-ruled island on a raft.
A fourth was taken to the U.S. military base at Guantanamo, southeast Cuba, where his appeal for political asylum will be assessed, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
The four were rescued by a Coast Guard cutter on Friday nine miles east of Alligator Reef in the Florida Keys.

Following a crisis in September 1994 when more than 30,000 Cubans tried to cross the straits to the United States, Washington announced in May 1995 (corrects from "last May") it would repatriate Cubans picked up at sea. The move ended a policy of virtual automatic asylum in the United States.
